note: Layouts are page STRUCTURES, independent of visual STYLE. Pick any style (KBS001-033) + any layout to get that style rendered in that page structure. Derived from KIBOOKAL Spread Production System v1.docx + Kibookal NOTEBOOK ENGINE.docx.
printable_rule: ABSOLUTE OUTPUT FORMAT — READ FIRST. Output a FLAT 2D DIGITAL ARTWORK FILE: only the printed graphic content itself, filling 100% of the frame and bleeding off all four edges. This is NOT a photograph of anything. DO NOT draw a notebook, book, journal, page object, paper sheet, binding, spine, stitching, curled corner, torn edge, drop shadow, vignette, frame, border, margin, mat, or ANY surrounding colour field / surface / desk / background behind or around it. There is NO object and NO scene — there is ONLY the artwork, edge to edge, like a full-bleed print-ready file. If the style is described as a notebook / journal / page / poster, render the CONTENT that would be printed, NOT the physical object, and let it fill every pixel to the edge.

layouts.name: Six-Layer Field Spread (A5+A5)
layouts.page_format: TWO A5 portrait pages side by side = one A4-landscape spread, with a visible centre gutter / spine fold. Each A5 half is a complete readable page; together one unified spread.
layouts.structure_block:
Lay the page out as a SIX-LAYER FIELD SPREAD across two A5 pages joined at a centre gutter:
  LAYER 1 ANCHOR — one dominant illustration of the subject, crossing the gutter to unify both pages.
  LAYER 2 FIELD NOTES — handwritten dual-register paragraphs (each line: a physical observation AND a philosophical/taxonomic conclusion), first-person investigator voice.
  LAYER 3 EVIDENCE — 5-8 found items (stamps, tickets, labels, fragments) with codes and official markings.
  LAYER 4 CLASSIFICATION BADGES — black-rectangle department header, circular archive stamp, yellow-highlighted key terms, red-caps intensifier, orange date box.
  LAYER 5 MICRO-MAP — a hand-drawn relational diagram with origin, destination, 3 waypoints, a distance and one anomaly.
  LAYER 6 VERDICT — a bold CASE STATUS stamp (OPEN / CLOSED / MISCLASSIFIED).
Six-level type hierarchy: large title caps → stamp-frame text → handwritten caps → flowing body → small technical annotations → marginal interjections. The page feels discovered, not designed.

layouts.name: Field Notebook Page (A5) — refined
layouts.page_format: ONE A5 portrait page (148×210mm), taller than wide.
layouts.structure_block:
Lay out a single A5-portrait FIELD NOTEBOOK page with EXCELLENT typographic hierarchy and varied text blocks. Use these distinct paragraph types, each visually different, with clear breathing room (never a wall of text):
  1. MASTHEAD (top): a LARGE hand-lettered TITLE + a small-caps line with a fake ARCHIVE CODE and DATE, separated by a thin rule.
  2. LEAD OBSERVATION: one flowing 3-4 line handwritten first-person paragraph in the investigator voice (observation + a small reflection).
  3. CENTRAL PLATE: the main illustration of the subject, with 4-6 tiny CALLOUT LABELS connected by fine curved arrows to specific parts.
  4. FIELD FACTS: a short bulleted list (3-5 bullets) of measurements / materials / traits — visually distinct from the flowing paragraph.
  5. CLASSIFICATION PANEL: a boxed, stamp-like block with CLASSIFICATION / RATING / STATUS lines.
  6. MARGINALIA: 2-3 small angular side-notes or corrections tucked in the margins (smallest text).
  7. PULL-QUOTE: one bold standout single line — an aphorism or verdict.
  8. CLOSING QUESTION: one strange UNANSWERED QUESTION in its own framed box at the bottom.
TYPOGRAPHY HIERARCHY (strict): title largest → section labels in small-caps with underline → handwritten body → micro callout-labels → marginalia smallest. Mix the block shapes (flowing paragraph, bullet list, boxed panel, marginal scrawl, framed question) so the page reads rich and designed-by-hand, not uniform.
Dense, intelligent, curious; a found page from a living world — discovered, not designed.

layouts.name: Object Study Page (A5)
layouts.structure_block:
Lay the page out as a single-A5 OBJECT STUDY:
  • ONE large object drawing (centre/top).
  • Measurements + material notes.
  • Possible use, and 2-3 crossed-out WRONG theories.
  • A small comparison sketch.
  • ONE final unresolved question.
Museum-record precision meets handmade field notes.

layouts.name: Creature / Asura Page (A5)
layouts.structure_block:
Lay the page out as a single-A5 CREATURE / ASURA observation page:
  • Creature name (hand-lettered title).
  • ONE main sketch of the creature.
  • Body notes + behaviour notes (labelled with arrows).
  • A weakness and a bad habit.
  • One comic observation in the margin.
  • A danger rating in an official badge.
Funny, intelligent, a little spooky but safe; discovered, not designed.

layouts.name: Museum Catalogue Page (A5)
layouts.structure_block:
Lay the page out as a single-A5 MUSEUM CATALOGUE:
  • Collection title.
  • A numbered grid of mini-drawings of the items.
  • A label + origin note under each.
  • A museum-style description.
  • One empty 'missing item' slot.
Orderly but handmade; archive-record feeling.

layouts.name: Map / Route Page (A5)
layouts.structure_block:
Lay the page out as a single-A5 MAP / ROUTE page:
  • A rough hand-drawn map filling most of the page.
  • A route line with waypoints.
  • Danger zones marked.
  • Found-object icons along the route.
  • A legend, an unreliable scale, and ONE impossible-geography note.
Relational not accurate; carries real data points.

layouts.name: Folk Devotional Plate (A5)
layouts.structure_block:
Compose a SINGLE devotional folk-art PLATE that fills the whole A5 page edge-to-edge:
  • The subject is the HERO, rendered fully in the chosen folk tradition's native composition (arch / border / banded mural / scroll / sculptural — per the style).
  • Integrate the subject's NAME as hand-lettering IN THE STYLE's own script/banner (small, tasteful) — no separate caption blocks.
  • NO field-notes, NO evidence stamps, NO classification boxes, NO verdict, NO arrows/callouts. This is a clean devotional painting, not an investigation page.
  • Traditional ornament fills the margins per the style; balanced, symmetrical where the tradition calls for it.
A finished folk-art plate you would frame — flat, printable, no background beyond the painting itself.

layouts.name: Pichwai Devi Spread
layouts.page_format: TWO A5 portrait pages side by side = one A4-landscape spread, thin painted centre gutter.
layouts.structure_block:
Two-A5 Pichwai spread inside one grand cusped golden temple-arch spanning both pages. ANCHOR deity centred crossing the gutter under a full moon; FIELD NOTES in gold-bordered cartouches in the side margins; EVIDENCE as small painted lotus/peacock medallions; CLASSIFICATION as a gold cartouche stamp; MICRO-MAP as a small mandala diagram; VERDICT as a temple-seal medallion. Deep indigo ground, dense gold ornament every margin.
FONT: ornate gold temple-display capitals for headers (Nathdwara devanagari-influenced), fine elegant serif for body; gold-outlined text cartouches.
Each A5 half is a complete readable page; page numbers in the bottom outer corners; all text readable at A5.

layouts.name: Dhokra Devi Plaque-Spread
layouts.page_format: TWO A5 portrait pages side by side = one A4-landscape spread, thin painted centre gutter.

Two-A5 Dhokra spread presented as a wall of cast-bronze relief panels. ANCHOR a large Dhokra figure of the deity centred; FIELD NOTES on small rectangular bronze plaques with embossed text; EVIDENCE as little cast-metal tokens; CLASSIFICATION on a bronze nameplate; MICRO-MAP as an engraved metal map; VERDICT on a stamped bronze seal. Warm patina, coiled-thread texture throughout.
FONT: cast-metal embossed relief lettering — raised bronze capitals for headers; captions on small bronze plaques. (Sculptural, not flat — Dhokra is metal craft.)
Each A5 half is a complete readable page; page numbers in the bottom outer corners; all text readable at A5.

layouts.name: Hand-drawn Diary Page (A5)
layouts.page_format: ONE A5 portrait page (148x210mm), full-bleed kraft/cream paper.
layouts.structure_block:
Lay out a single CHILD-S HAND-DRAWN DIARY page on warm kraft/cream paper (intimate personal journal, NOT a printed magazine):
  - A big hand-lettered TITLE or date at the top in a kid-s hand.
  - The DIARY ENTRY as flowing first-person HANDWRITTEN text in a main column (readable at A5).
  - A central or corner ILLUSTRATION/SKETCH that depicts the entry - pencil plus light watercolour doodle - with small CALLOUT annotations and curved arrows labelling parts.
  - Scattered MARGINAL DOODLES (little objects, creatures, clouds) with tiny handwritten captions.
  - A small WHAT-IF musing cluster or a blank/lined journal box.
  - A few sideways margin notes.
  All hand-drawn, loose and imperfect, warm and personal; page number small in a corner. Everything readable at A5.

layouts.name: Kibookal Master Diary Page (A5) — maximalist
layouts.page_format: ONE A5 portrait page (148x210mm), full-bleed warm kraft/cream diary paper.
layouts.structure_block:
Compose the RICHEST possible Kibookal diary page - a discovery-dense, layered hand-drawn journal page where a child reads it once for the story, twice for the doodles, three times for the hidden meaning. On warm kraft/cream paper, hand-drawn, intimate, NOT a printed magazine. Layer these zones (arrange organically, overlapping like a real busy journal, generous but readable):
  1. MASTHEAD: a big hand-lettered TITLE + the day/date + a tiny weather-or-mood doodle (sun, cloud, storm-in-the-tummy).
  2. THE ENTRY: the flowing first-person HANDWRITTEN diary text - the heart of the page, clearly readable.
  3. HERO SKETCH: one central pencil-and-light-watercolour scene of the day, with curved CALLOUT arrows + tiny annotations naming parts.
  4. DEVI-OF-THE-DAY: a small framed emblem badge naming which of the nine Devis the writer became today (e.g. Today I was Kalaratri) with a 3-word reason.
  5. THE EVOLVING FRIEND: a recurring small corner caricature of Arjun that grows a little more accurate/kind each page (a running visual thread across the diary).
  6. WHAT-IF CLUSTER: 3-5 scattered tiny what-if musings in small hand, each with a mini-doodle.
  7. MARGIN DOODLES: little objects/creatures from the day with one-word labels tucked in the margins.
  8. PRESSED ARTIFACT: a taped ticket, pressed leaf, temple stamp or coin - proof the day happened.
  9. BEEJA / VIBRATION CORNER: a small Om or beeja-mantra doodle with wavy vibration lines - the inner thread.
 10. SECRET CONFESSION: a tiny boxed honest aside in the kid voice (A confession:).
 11. INSIDE/OUTSIDE micro-panel: a tiny split sketch showing the day-s outer event mirrored as an inner feeling (battles outside = battles within).
 12. TOMORROW SEED: a one-line tomorrow I want to... at the bottom, plus a small page number.
Unity from one hand, one kraft paper, one warm palette. Layered and busy but every layer readable at A5. Maximum charm and things-to-discover.

INVISIBLE STRUCTURE — CRITICAL: the zone names above (MASTHEAD, ENTRY, HERO SKETCH, DEVI-OF-THE-DAY, EVOLVING FRIEND, BEEJA, SECRET CONFESSION, INSIDE/OUTSIDE, MARGIN DOODLES, TOMORROW SEED, etc.) are layout instructions ONLY. NEVER print these zone names as headers or labels on the page. The page shows only the diary-s own hand-lettered title and natural handwritten content — like a real journal, with no design-zone captions.
